slides.notes:
PHASE 2 · PROTECT
The Seven Sins of Isolation
Memorize them. Laminate them. Audit yourself against them.
1 No lip protection — vitamin E or vaseline
2 Wrong retractor for the system
3 No filtered eye protection
4 Barrier not properly placed or cured
5 Not enough whitening gel (below 1 mm)
6 Patient left unattended — no signal agreed
7 Dentin sensitivity not managed
CLINICAL FOCUS: Burns are never caused by the gel. Rescue: vitamin E or vaseline onto the gingiva — no panic, protocol.

slides.title: 1 mm. Green. Neutral pH.

points.text: Mixed fresh, full potency until use.
Every surface visibly covered.
Chromogens oxidised at neutral pH.

slides.notes:
PHASE 3 · APPLY
1 mm. Green. Neutral pH.
The gel is engineered for precision — starve it and you starve the result.
Dual-chamber 32% HP. Mix fresh — full potency protected until the moment of mixing.
Green = precision. You see every surface covered — the gel turns clear as oxygen releases.
Oxidation, not erosion. Whitens by oxidation of chromogens at a neutral pH — never by corroding the enamel surface.
Minimum 1 mm, everywhere. A thin, starved layer produces a pale patch — Sin #5.

slides.title: The Lamp: Position Is Power

points.text: Patient at 45°, lamp head locked on the retractor — intensity level IIII.
One centimetre of gap costs ≈50% of the power.
Blue 460 nm light, absorbed by the green gel — no UV, no infrared, below 39 °C.

chart.title: Light power at the enamel
chart.note: 1 cm of extra gap ≈ 50% less light power (3² = 9 vs 4² = 16)

slides.notes:
PHASE 3 · APPLY
The Lamp: Position Is Power
Light intensity falls with the square of distance — respect the physics.
Lock the geometry. Patient at 45°; lamp head easy-locked onto the fläsh retractor — confirm intensity level IIII.
The expensive centimetre. One centimetre of gap costs ≈50% of the power (3² = 9 → 4² = 16).
Complementary-colour activation. Blue 460 nm light is absorbed by the green gel — a photochemical effect, not heat.
Up to 30% lighter, safely. No UV, no infrared, below 39 °C — the light drives the chemistry, it never warms the tooth.
1 cm of extra gap ≈ 50% less light power. Ontiveros & Paravina, J Dent 2009.

slides.title: The Aftercare Window

points.text: No magic number — make chromogen-light choices while the pellicle re-establishes.
Slight settling over the next days is normal — say it in the chair.

slides.notes:
PHASE 5 · SEAL & INSTRUCT
The Aftercare Window
What you say in the next sixty seconds decides this week’s phone calls.
The pellicle rebuilds fast. A basal layer forms within minutes; near-full thickness by ~2 hours; maturation over ~18–24 hours in vivo.
Mind the first hours. Not a magic number — the rigid “48-hour” rule is weakly evidenced; make chromogen-light choices while the pellicle re-establishes.
Pre-empt the rebound. Today’s shade is partly dehydration-enhanced; slight settling over days is normal — say it in the chair.
The departure gift. fläsh Whitening Toothpaste with every patient — premium aftercare, your clinic on their shelf.
EVIDENCE: Hannig M. Ultrastructural investigation of pellicle morphogenesis over a 24-h period. Clin Oral Investig. 1999;3(2):88–95.

slides.title: “The Uneven Case”
slides.story: A 38-year-old at the end of cycle 3 — centrals magnificent, cervical thirds still yellow, canines two steps behind, chalky patches on the laterals. She is holding the mirror.

findings.cause: Gel layer below 1 mm in zones — Sin #5
Lamp gap or tilt — 1 cm ≈ −50% power

slides.notes:
MINI CASE
“The Uneven Case”
A 38-year-old at the end of cycle 3 — centrals magnificent, cervical thirds still yellow, canines two steps behind, chalky patches on the laterals. She is holding the mirror.
MINI CASE · DIAGNOSE
The Troubleshooting Checklist
Run the checklist — never guess in front of the patient.
Cervical thirds still yellow. Barrier over-extended onto cervical enamel — the gel never touched it.
Patchy brightness. Gel layer below 1 mm in zones — Sin #5.
Everything underperforming. Lamp gap or tilt — remember: 1 cm ≈ −50% power.
Biology, not error. Canines (thicker dentin) are always slowest; chalky patches are transient dehydration over hypocalcifications.
Chalky white patches. transient dehydration revealing hypocalcifications (not damage)
CLINICAL FOCUS: Five findings. Five causes. Zero mystery.

steps.title: Re-isolate, correctly
steps.text: Rebuild the barrier and confirm the retractor is docked on the lamp head.

steps.title: Fresh 1 mm gel
steps.text: Full-thickness layer on the canines and cervical thirds — the lagging zones.

steps.title: Spend banked minutes
steps.text: The cycle time the fläshcard saved becomes a targeted touch-up.

steps.title: Say the words
steps.text: “The canines are always last. The white areas are temporary.” Book the one-week photo.

slides.notes:
MINI CASE · RESOLVE
The Fix & The Conversation
1 Re-isolate, correctly. Rebuild the barrier properly and confirm the retractor is docked on the lamp head.
2 Fresh 1 mm gel. Full-thickness layer on the canines and cervical thirds — the lagging zones.
3 Spend banked minutes. The cycle time the fläshcard saved becomes a targeted touch-up — the closed-but-flexible system pays you back.
4 Say the words. “The canines are always last — normal biology. The white areas are temporary dehydration.” Book the one-week photo before she leaves.
